semantic_atoms.finding: The donor explicitly separates model-generated cognition from canonical DB/effect authority; Stern is the control/writer boundary in the checked source region.
semantic_atoms.boundary: The stronger repository-wide claim that no other executable file writes canonical state is not yet proven by this span and remains an open writer-audit question.

semantic_atoms.finding: UnifiedDB path resolution and runtime dependency resolution are authority-bearing integration surfaces; migration must pin concrete DB identity and dependency reachability rather than infer them from filenames.
Dynamic/runtime dependency paths make static deletion of apparently redundant donor files unsafe without reachability evidence.

Voice uses reusable arbitration/scoring and loop-control primitives. These are migration candidates for a shared GRID/voice/visual arbitration ABI; any local-model output remains candidate cognition rather than state/effect authority.

Visual Cortex participates in the same arbitration/perception family. External semantic vision is an optional perception mechanism, not a canonical truth path, and must remain capability-gated under current provider hard-off.

The donor distinguishes observed evidence, inferred hypotheses and retrieval priors. These distinctions are directly reusable as Typed Entry epistemic classes if provenance, generation and confidence remain explicit.
CaptureWorker implements one camera owner per process, multi-reader FrameRefs, bounded RAM buffering, monotonic ordering/TTL and a no-raw-frame-disk-write architecture for the continuous path.
semantic_atoms.boundary: The lock is process-local; cross-process single ownership requires a stronger lease/OS/device coordination primitive before Physical-GRID10 claims.

architecture_deltas.delta: Converge voice, visual and GRID arbitration onto one shared typed arbitration ABI instead of creating module-specific truth or decision authorities.
Map observed, inferred and retrieval-prior perceptual atoms into Typed Entry with explicit provenance, generation, confidence and causal identity.
Retain a single capture-owner/multi-consumer pattern for camera input. Upgrade process-local ownership to a cross-process lease before multi-process GRID10 assembly.
Keep semantic provider vision optional and hard-gated. Base perception liveness and local state production must survive with all external provider routes disabled.
Preserve Stern/EffectGate-style deterministic effect authority: voice, visual, models and J-Space may produce candidates but cannot directly mint canonical state or real effects.
Require source/runtime reachability evidence before deleting donor files that appear redundant; dynamic imports and compatibility paths must be treated as potentially live until disproven.

preserved_contradictions.claim_a: stern.py presents itself as the canonical DB writer/control authority.
preserved_contradictions.claim_b: Repository-wide exclusivity has not yet been established by an exhaustive writer audit.
preserved_contradictions.falsifier: Enumerate executable canonical-state writers at the pinned donor commit and prove all non-Stern writes are projections, historical, tests, or gated through the same authority.

preserved_contradictions.claim_a: Donor visual code contains provider-capable semantic vision paths and historical provider test references.
preserved_contradictions.claim_b: Current canonical supervisor inbox requires provider hard-off/quiescence and grants zero provider-route runtime credit.
preserved_contradictions.resolution: Retain provider-capable code only as historical/optional donor capability; no current provider execution or runtime credit is implied.

preserved_contradictions.claim_a: CaptureWorker enforces single owner of the camera.
preserved_contradictions.claim_b: Its owner set and lock are process-local and therefore do not prove cross-process ownership for a physical GRID10 deployment.
preserved_contradictions.falsifier: Demonstrate a cross-process device lease/lock with stale-owner recovery and exact process identity binding.
